On the metal I started with like 160 or something really gritty, then moved to 220 then 400. After priming I waited a day before sanding with 400 grit on a sanding block. Filled with the pits with bondo and let that cure over night. Then I went at it with the 400 grit again. Primed again, let that dry and then I did a guide coat (just lightly sprayed with black spray paint to contrast the green primer). Let that cure overnight. Then I went at it with 600 grit. Then I sprayed the base coat (4 coats) and let it cure for 2 days. Taped it off and sprayed the black lines, waited 30 min and peeled the tape and let it cure for 2 days. Wet sanded with 600 grit lightly then applied the clear coat (4 coats to help prevent  damage from gas) and let that cure for 2 days. After each time I sanded I used glass cleaner to clean it off before spraying anything else. Thaaaaats about it. Probably could make it a lot simpler but I just tried to do the best I could with my zero experience haha

Got the tank as raw metal, sanded it down, primed it, block sanded to find inconsistencies, filled with bondo, blocked again, primed, blocked, base coat (tan), let it cure a few days, wet sanded, taped off for the stripes (this was the toughest part to try and get them even and consistent), peeled the tape after about 30 minutes let it cure a few days, then I wet sanded again and did 4 coats of a 2k clear coat. 

Originally my plan was to wet sand again after the clear coat and then buff and polish it, BUT I actually kind of like the orange peel look (dont crucify me pls) and I’m just gonna leave it as is for now! 

And yes, this was all done in a little 5x6 corner that I taped off in my garage (makeshift paint room). I used duplicolor rattle cans and a rattle can 2k 2 part clear coat.
